clue.text: Quietly made call holding a knife

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it inside your grasp, so the pieces before this word take the next one inside them

parts.note: P, for piano, is the marking in sheet music that means quietly
rang is the past tense of ring, to telephone someone

explanation.surface: Someone discreetly telephoned while gripping a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' makes P and RANG together take the A inside, landing between them. A parang is the heavy machete of Malaysia and Indonesia.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a heavy, machete-like blade carried in Malaysia and Indonesia for clearing jungle.

clue.text: Some grasp endangered tree

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few people understand that a species of tree is under threat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' asks for part of what follows: the answer runs across the gap between 'grasp' and 'endangered'.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a slender poplar whose leaves tremble in the lightest breeze.

clue.text: Desperate Dan's very game etc

indicators.note: a desperate person acts wildly, which tells you the letters of the name beside it are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the name Dan supplies its three letters; the possessive 's adds nothing
so means very, as in 'so kind of you'
someone who is game for a plan is on for it: both mean willing

explanation.surface: The stubbly cowboy from the comics is extremely willing, among other things.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is the stubbly strongman of the British comic The Dandy, so 'Desperate' reads as part of his name; it is the anagram signal, turning DAN into AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both tell you a list continues in the same way, 'etc' being short for the Latin et cetera.

clue.text: Italian patriot makes gesture at first — a rude one

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it, the way a word begins

parts.note: ribald means coarsely or indecently humorous, so rude
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A hero of Italy's unification opens proceedings with an obscene hand signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes only the opening letter of 'gesture'. The dash is punctuation for the surface, and 'makes' simply joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Giuseppe, the nineteenth-century general whose Redshirt volunteers fought to unify Italy.

clue.text: An Athenian with an unknown element

parts.note: Timon is the title character of Shakespeare's play Timon of Athens
in algebra an unknown quantity is written x, y or z; here it is y

explanation.surface: A citizen of Athens is carrying a substance nobody can identify.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Athenian' is not any Greek but Shakespeare's Timon of Athens. The second 'an' belongs with 'unknown', an algebra letter, so the 'unknown element' of the surface is split between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the brittle, silvery metalloid with symbol Sb and atomic number 51.

clue.text: Display caviare evenly

indicators.note: evenly asks for the letters at even positions in the word before it: the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Spread the fish roe out on the plate in a neat, level layer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evenly' is an instruction, not a description of the spreading: keep the second, fourth and sixth letters of 'caviare'. 'Display' is a verb, as when you air your views.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to voice or parade something publicly, as you do with an opinion or a grievance.

clue.text: At centre of bank you can see its first flower

indicators.note: whatever is at the centre of a thing sits in its exact middle, so one piece goes into the middle of the word for bank

parts.note: a bank of seats or of switches is a tier, a row set in ranks

indicators.note: its looks back to the word bank, and first takes that word's opening letter

explanation.surface: Halfway along the riverside you can spot the first bloom of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is something that flows, a river: here Rome's. 'its first' is the first letter of 'bank' itself, and 'At centre of' places it in the middle of TIER, a bank of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-only sense: read as flow-er, a thing that flows, it describes the river running through Rome.

clue.text: Idiot holding laurel's horse

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it in your grasp, so the word for idiot has the comedian's name inside it

parts.note: mug is British slang for a fool, someone easily taken in
Stan Laurel was the thin half of the film comedy duo Laurel and Hardy; the possessive 's adds nothing

explanation.surface: Some fool is minding the horse that belongs to Laurel.
explanation.walkthrough: Lower-case 'laurel' looks like the plant but is a surname: the thin half of the film comedians Laurel and Hardy. 'holding' puts his first name inside a British slang word for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the free-roaming feral breed of the American West, descended from Spanish stock.

clue.text: Where finally, Gordon brown has rather short tenure?

definitions.text: Where finally, Gordon brown has rather short tenure?

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of the name that comes next

parts.note: umber is a brown earth pigment, as in burnt umber

indicators.note: rather short says the word tenure stops well before its end, dropping more than a single letter

parts.note: the last three letters of tenure, the part that is cut off

explanation.surface: A dig at the former prime minister: where, in the end, did he serve only a brief spell?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: Gordon Brown was British prime minister for under three years, living at 10 Downing Street. 'finally' takes the last letter of Gordon and 'rather short' trims TENURE to TEN; lower-case 'brown' is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole-clue description: the prime minister's official residence is 10 Downing Street, where Brown lived for just under three years.

clue.text: Bread and endless crisps scattered around shellfish

indicators.note: things scattered around lie strewn out of place, so the letters before these words are put in a new order
endless means without an end, so the word after it drops its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of crisps, the one that is dropped

explanation.surface: A picnic of bread and unlimited crisps lies strewn round a plate of seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' is not 'unlimited': it removes the last letter of 'crisps' (British for potato chips), leaving CRISP. 'scattered around' then rearranges BREAD plus CRISP, with 'and' only joining the two.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a long-legged marine crustacean, caught and eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Wrestling with problem of lacking female

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem set for schoolchildren

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the word before it gives up the letter that the next word stands for

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for female, as on forms

explanation.surface: A man is struggling with the difficulty of having no woman in his life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrestling with' reads as struggling over a difficulty, but 'Wrestling' alone is the definition. 'lacking' takes F (female) out of 'of', leaving O after SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the Japanese sport in which two heavyweights try to force each other out of a ring.

clue.text: When abroad, one business looking strange

parts.note: un is the French word for one; 'when abroad' asks you to translate it
Co is the abbreviation for company, which is a business

explanation.surface: On a trip overseas, a particular company appears distinctly odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When abroad' asks for a foreign word: the French for one is UN. The answer is Scots, best known from the phrase 'the unco guid' for the self-righteous.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in Scots dialect: the word means odd, unusual or remarkable.

clue.text: Looking silly if beard cut in two parts

indicators.note: something that looks silly is not in its proper shape, so the letters after these words are put in a different order

parts.note: these ten letters are the material to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man would look ridiculous with his beard trimmed into two separate halves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looking silly' is the anagram signal for IF BEARD CUT. The surface describes a forked beard, which is just what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something that has forked is divided into a pair of branches.

clue.text: Soft soap and cloth

definitions.meaning: soft soap is flattery or smooth persuasive talk, and so, in British slang, is this word
a soft woven woollen fabric, and in Britain also the small square of towelling used to wash your face

explanation.surface: Two things you would find beside the bathroom basin.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions joined by 'and'. In Britain a flannel is a face cloth, and 'flannel' is also slang for the smooth, flattering talk that 'soft soap' means.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday British English: smooth, flattering talk, and a woollen fabric or washcloth.

clue.text: Very acidic substance — ph 1 — returned to head of lab

parts.note: the two letters are used as they stand; the surface dresses them as the acidity scale

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word for the numeral is written from its last letter to its first

parts.note: the numeral 1 written out as a word is one

indicators.note: the head of something is its top or front, so this takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A fiercely corrosive chemical, measuring pH 1, was sent back to the laboratory's boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes and the pH reading are surface dressing: 'ph' gives its two letters as written. 'returned' turns ONE (the numeral 1 spelt out) into ENO, and 'head of' takes the first letter of 'lab'.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: also called carbolic acid, it is a corrosive compound, though chemists rate it only weakly acidic.

clue.text: Alternative practitioner in course about principle of organon

indicators.note: about means around, so the two pieces before it stand on either side of the letter that follows

parts.note: someone who is in is at home, as when a caller asks if the doctor is in
a course is a route or path, the way something travels

indicators.note: principle is used loosely in its old sense of a beginning or source, so this takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A complementary therapist is taking a class on the founding idea of a classic text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a container signal here: someone who is in is at home. 'about' is the signal, and 'principle of' picks the first letter of 'organon', the title of Hahnemann's founding text of this alternative medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: someone practising a branch of complementary medicine that uses extremely diluted remedies.

clue.text: Get rid of tea bag or get another blend of it

indicators.note: a blend is a mixture, and it points back to the three words just before, so their letters are mixed into a different order

parts.note: these eight letters, the word or included, are the material to be mixed

explanation.surface: Throw the tea bag away, or else try a different variety of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a choice between two actions but is part of the letters: 'get another blend of it' rearranges TEA BAG OR, with 'it' pointing back at those three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to repeal or formally abolish a law or agreement is to do away with it.

clue.text: How one is greeted at a party

definitions.meaning: the way a person or an idea is received, warmly or coolly, by those who meet it
a formal social gathering, such as the one that follows a wedding

explanation.surface: The welcome a guest receives on arriving at a social gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions with 'at' between them: the welcome a person gets, and the formal party held after a wedding. The surface runs them together as one smooth phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the manner in which someone is welcomed, and a formal social gathering.

clue.text: Old embassy is something that's been neglected

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old, as in OT for Old Testament
a diplomatic mission is an embassy, a country's permanent delegation abroad

explanation.surface: A former diplomatic building has been left to fall into disrepair.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface shows a run-down building, but 'is' simply equates the wordplay with the definition: something left out or left undone.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a thing left out, or a duty not carried out, is what the noun names.

clue.text: Band I note is a possible accompaniment to 26

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn round the waist or over one shoulder
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale: do, re, mi

explanation.surface: A group of musicians that I spot could be the supporting act for number 26.
explanation.walkthrough: '26' points to the answer at 26 across, a Japanese drink that this dish of sliced raw fish might go with. 'Band' is a strip of cloth, not musicians, and 'note' is a sol-fa syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: thin slices of raw fish, a Japanese dish often served with the rice wine at 26 across.

clue.text: What binds religious chaps at front of temple

parts.note: CE is the Church of England; the adjective is a loose pointer to the church, as in a CE school
chaps is informal British English for men

indicators.note: the front of a word is where it begins, so this takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Something unites the devout men gathered at the entrance to a temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'religious' points to the Church of England, CE, so 'religious chaps' are CE MEN. 'at front of' takes the first letter of 'temple'.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a building material that sets hard and sticks bricks together, and figuratively anything that unites people.

clue.text: We hear senior officer relating to soldiers

indicators.note: we hear says the word for the officer is to be listened to and not read: what counts is how it is pronounced

parts.note: a marshal is a very high military rank; a field marshal is the top rank of the British Army

explanation.surface: Word reaches us of a high-ranking commander telling the troops a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' makes it a soundalike: MARSHAL, as in field marshal, the British Army's top rank, is pronounced the same as the answer but spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the adjective describes anything military or warlike, from combat arts to army law.

clue.text: Batter fish first — then start to season tripe

indicators.note: first says the fish goes at the front, ahead of the word for batter that the clue gives before it
then says the next piece follows straight after the fish, which leaves the word for batter to come last

parts.note: cod is a common food fish, the staple of British fish and chips

indicators.note: the start to a word is its opening letter, here of the word that follows

parts.note: to batter is to hit hard and repeatedly, to wallop

explanation.surface: A chip-shop recipe: coat the fish before you begin flavouring the offal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a fish-and-chip-shop recipe, but 'Batter' means hit hard and 'tripe' means nonsense, not offal. 'first' sends the fish to the front, 'then' adds the 'start to' letter of 'season', and the hitting word comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in British slang: both words mean nonsense or rubbish.

clue.text: Pointless request to umpire is to cause dismay

indicators.note: read as point-less: the next piece gives up a point of the compass, which is a single letter

parts.note: in cricket the fielding side makes an appeal to the umpire, asking for the batsman to be given out
E is east, one of the four points of the compass

explanation.surface: A futile shout to the cricket official is bound to upset people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointless' is not 'futile' but 'without a point': removing a compass point, E for east, from APPEAL. In cricket, fielders appeal to the umpire for a batsman to be given out.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to horrify or shock someone deeply, filling them with consternation.

clue.text: Clobber royal gong

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RAF, the Royal Air Force
gong is British slang for a medal; the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is an honour awarded by the monarch

explanation.surface: Somebody gives the palace's ceremonial gong a mighty whack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' is not a blow but British slang for clothes. 'gong' is British slang for a medal: the OBE, an honour awarded by the monarch, follows R for royal.
explanation.definitionFit: An example in British slang: clobber means clothing or gear, and a long loose gown is one item of it.

clue.text: Irish rock star carries German drum

indicators.note: to carry something is to bear it within, so the singer's name has the next piece inside it

parts.note: Bono is the stage name of Paul Hewson, lead singer of the Dublin band U2
G is the abbreviation for German, as in dictionaries

explanation.surface: A famous singer from Ireland lugs a percussion instrument made in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' is the container signal: BONO, singer of the Dublin band U2, takes G for German inside. The surface suggests a German-made instrument, but 'drum' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: one of a pair of small Cuban hand drums played with the fingers.

clue.text: Runner without a drink in Tokyo

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, as in 'without the city walls', so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a ski is a runner, a long blade that slides over snow

explanation.surface: An athlete in the Japanese capital has nothing to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' does not mean lacking: in its old sense of outside, it puts SKI, a runner on snow, round A. The answer is a variant spelling of sake, Japanese rice wine.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a variant spelling of sake, the Japanese rice wine.

clue.text: Nice profit can be made from having great facility

indicators.note: these words say the two words before them can be built out of the letters of the word defined, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: these ten letters are the material to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A healthy return can be earned by owning a first-rate building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be made from' is the anagram signal, read from the far side: NICE PROFIT can be made from the letters of the answer. 'facility' is not a building here but ease or skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: facility here means ease or skill, so someone with plenty of it is highly competent.

clue.text: Blade chopping head off pig

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so chopping it off removes that letter from the next piece

parts.note: a boar is a male pig, wild or farmed
the opening letter of the word for pig, the one that is removed

explanation.surface: A knife is used to behead a hog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopping head off' removes the first letter of BOAR, a male pig. 'Blade' is not a knife: rowers call the flat end of an oar, and the whole oar, a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in rowing: the flat end that dips in the water lends its name to the whole implement.

clue.text: One working the land taking an hour to get best-selling album

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the word for the farm worker has the next piece inside it

parts.note: to till is to plough and prepare the soil, so a tiller is a person who works the land
hr is the standard abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: A farmhand needs sixty minutes to go and buy a chart-topping record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is the container signal, not a measure of time: the farm worker takes the abbreviation inside. The album is Michael Jackson's 1982 record, the best-selling of all time, and 'to get' just joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Michael Jackson's 1982 record, the biggest-selling album ever released.

clue.text: Hold mariner with dodgy vision

definitions.meaning: a wrestling grip in which an arm goes under the opponent's arm from behind and the hand presses on the neck
the British admiral who won the Battle of Trafalgar in 1805 had lost the sight of his right eye

explanation.surface: Grab on to the sailor whose eyesight can't be trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions side by side. Horatio Nelson, Britain's naval hero of Trafalgar, was blind in one eye, and a nelson is also a wrestling hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses share the name: a wrestling grip on the neck, and Britain's one-eyed admiral of Trafalgar.
